status: Analysis design fixed before computing these new history contrasts; not an external preregistration.
question: Do equal-duration, equal-peak, equal-dose demand programs leave different finite-window or terminal states under unchanged model coefficients?
coefficient_rule: Reuse the existing six-equation nominal stationary construction without coefficient changes or outcome-based searches.

post_history_relaxation.rule: Continue all seven coordinates from the finest-grid endpoint under unchanged basal forcing; classify against stationary references from the same direction and coefficient set. Retain unresolved runs.

feedback_subsets.frozen_rule: For each direction every inactive coordinate is frozen at the same full-system starting reference. All sixteen subsets and all three histories are retained. Each subset defines a different vector field; terminal states are compared only within that subset.
feedback_subsets.interpretation: Finite-history dependence and within-subset distinct stationary outcomes; not proof that seven coordinates are mathematically necessary.

interpretation.hysteresis_claim: Equal-dose history effects alone do not establish rate-independent hysteresis. Distinct recorded terminal states require small active-field residuals and a distance exceeding the fixed classification tolerance within one unchanged vector field.
interpretation.design_scope: Programs share peak, total high duration, total observation time and final high-demand end. Their earlier timing and maximum uninterrupted duration differ jointly; a difference is a schedule effect, not an isolated universal effect of number of interruptions.

scalar_comparator.amendment: Added before comparator effects were computed, following the primary-source review: a stable scalar lag can produce finite-window schedule differences without multiple equilibria. All fixed time constants retained without fitting.
scalar_comparator.terminal_equilibrium: basal external_demand, identical for all histories

exploratory_duration_extension.status: EXPLORATORY amendment after reading the initial 20-high-unit primary result; not prespecified confirmatory evidence.
exploratory_duration_extension.reason: All three initial aligned histories returned to the upper reference. Check whether that null terminal contrast depends on the chosen duration, without changing amplitude, coefficients or selecting a successful condition.
exploratory_duration_extension.histories: all three histories at every scale
exploratory_duration_extension.inference: Compare schedules only within each fixed duration/dose level; differences across duration levels also change total exposure. Retain every result including nulls.
